# Continue Watching Service (`eyevinn-continue-watching-api`)

A user of a streaming service expects that they can pick up where they left on any of their devices. To handle that you would need to develop a service with endpoints for the application to write and read from. This open source cloud component take care of that and all you need is to have a Redis database running on Redis Cloud for example.

[Service documentation](https://dev.to/video/how-to-quickly-setup-a-continue-watching-endpoint-for-your-video-players-ek7) · [Source](https://github.com/Eyevinn/continue-watching-api)

## Example

```terraform
resource "osc_instance" "example" {
  service_id = "eyevinn-continue-watching-api"
  name       = "myapi"

  parameters = {
    RedisHost     = "..."
    # RedisPort     = "..."
    # RedisUsername = "..."
    # RedisPassword = "..."
  }
}
```

Commented lines are optional parameters. Values marked `"..."` need a real value. Outputs are `url`, `external_ip`, `external_port` and the raw `instance` document, see the `osc_instance` resource.

## Parameters

| Name | Type | Required | Description |
|---|---|---|---|
| `RedisHost` | string | yes | URL endpoint for external service |
| `RedisPort` | string | no | Port number for the service to listen on |
| `RedisUsername` | string | no | Configuration option for redisusername |
| `RedisPassword` | string | no | Configuration option for redispassword |

The instance `name` must match `^\w+$` and be unique per service within the workspace. OSC lowercases it and allows at most 20 characters.

Parameter values are strings; booleans take `"true"` or `"false"`. Reference an `osc_secret` as `osc_secret.<name>.ref` to keep a value out of the instance configuration. This page is generated from the OSC catalog; the provider validates against the live catalog when planning.
